import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 43

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/43](https://www.erdosproblems.com/43)
-/

open scoped Pointwise

namespace Erdos43

/--
Let $f(N)$ be the maximum possible size of a Sidon set in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$.
-/
noncomputable abbrev f (N : ℕ) : ℕ := Finset.maxSidonSubsetCard (Finset.Icc 1 N)

/--
If $A$ and $B$ are Sidon sets in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with
$(A-A)\cap(B-B)=\{0\}$, is it true that
$$\binom{\lvert A\rvert}{2}+\binom{\lvert B\rvert}{2}\leq\binom{f(N)}{2}+O(1)?$$

The answer is no; the Erdős Problems page notes that this follows from the solution to
Erdős Problem 42.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_43.parts.i : answer(False) ↔
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ N in Filter.atTop, ∀ (A B : Finset ℕ),
      A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N →
      B ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N →
      IsSidon (A : Set ℕ) →
      IsSidon (B : Set ℕ) →
      (A - A) ∩ (B - B) = {0} →
      ((A.card.choose 2 + B.card.choose 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ ((f N).choose 2 : ℝ) + C := by
  sorry

/--
If $A$ and $B$ are equal-sized Sidon sets in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with
$(A-A)\cap(B-B)=\{0\}$, can the bound be improved to
$$\binom{\lvert A\rvert}{2}+\binom{\lvert B\rvert}{2}
    \leq (1-c+o(1))\binom{f(N)}{2}$$
for some constant $c>0$?

The answer is no; the Erdős Problems page records a negative answer due to Barreto.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_43.parts.ii : answer(False) ↔
    ∃ᵉ (c > 0), ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, o =o[Filter.atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧
    ∀ᶠ N in Filter.atTop, ∀ (A B : Finset ℕ),
      A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N →
      B ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N →
      IsSidon (A : Set ℕ) →
      IsSidon (B : Set ℕ) →
      A.card = B.card →
      (A - A) ∩ (B - B) = {0} →
      ((A.card.choose 2 + B.card.choose 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤
        (1 - c + o N) * ((f N).choose 2 : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos43

reformulations.difference: The difference-set hypothesis uses truncated subtraction on ℕ rather than the signed integer differences implicit in the source.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every pair of natural-number finsets A and B, the Lean equality is equivalent to the same equality for their images in ℤ. For a nonempty set, truncated self-differences are exactly the nonnegative signed self-differences. Signed self-difference sets are symmetric, so a common negative difference also gives a common positive difference. If either set is empty, equality to {0} fails in both interpretations. Proved the exact equivalence as nat_diff_iff_int_diff in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean, including its preservation under arbitrary propositional contexts.

reformulations.difference: The equal-size variant likewise uses truncated natural-number subtraction in its difference-set hypothesis.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The same proved equivalence applies to all A and B, without requiring Sidon or cardinality hypotheses. Consequently it remains valid after imposing equal cardinalities and under the existential c/o quantifiers, eventual universal bound, and negative-answer context in this declaration.

review.notes: Checked all three declarations. The source states both displayed bounds exactly as formalized and records negative answers to both, agreeing with answer(False) and research solved. The definition of f is an attained maximum over all Sidon subsets, not merely an inclusion-maximal size; attainment and its upper-bound property were proved in scratch. Computations gave f(0),…,f(8) = 0,1,2,2,3,3,3,4,4. Empty sets fail the difference hypothesis in both interpretations, while singleton pairs provide admissible inputs for every N ≥ 1. Checked the uniform quantifier scopes, real-valued bounds, binomial coefficients, and little-o semantics. Also proved that allowing an arbitrary real C instead of requiring C > 0 does not change the upper O(1) claim. Both /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/equivalences.lean compile without errors. No repository files were edited.
